commodity: Value clothing and general merchandise retail (multi-site)
operations: Ackermans and PEP are divisions of JSE-listed Pepkor Holdings (head office 36 Stellenberg Road Parow Industria). Group footprint 6 158 stores at 30 Sep 2025 (PEP 2 693 incl. PEP Home 468; Ackermans 1 036; Pepkor Speciality 977; Lifestyle 925). Stores mostly leased; solar sits on owned buildings, DCs, hubs and head offices. Acquired Legit/Swagga/Style (469 stores) Nov 2025 and OK Furniture/House & Home non-RSA stores Oct 2025.
scale_note: 12 MWp solar PV installed across 64 completed sites (R97m invested) generating 5 197 MWh in FY25 (~R12m/yr saving); 2.6 MWp added in FY25; a further 3.6 MWp to be added in FY26 via bilateral electricity wheeling; R280m energy-efficiency roll-out planned FY25-FY28; grid electricity 216 734 MWh in FY25 (-7% yoy); Ackermans invested R28.4m in solar; LED retrofits saved 22 257 MWh since 2019. No published net-zero date; Scope 2 is the largest emission source.

operations: Two separate JSE-listed companies bundled in this record. Cashbuild Ltd (HO 2 Handel Road Ormonde Johannesburg): 318 stores across 6 countries at 29 June 2025 (Cashbuild + P&L Hardware), 5 357 employees; stores trade 07:00-18:00 so the load is daytime. Italtile Ltd (HO 72 Peter Place Bryanston): 165 SA retail stores (13 Italtile, 67 CTM, 85 TopT) plus 19 rest-of-Africa stores; also owns the Ceramic Industries factories - the large industrial load sits in manufacturing not retail.
scale_note: Cashbuild: electricity consumed 15.5 GWh FY25 (metered stores only, prepaid excluded); solar PV at Support Office (Oct 2024) and Corporate Office (Jun 2025); solar-plus-battery pilots at some stores; 290 stores on LED/low-voltage induction lighting; auto-start diesel generator at every store (14.23 MWth installed thermal capacity). No wheeling or PPA published. Italtile: group generated over 8 000 MWh of solar power in 2024 (largely at factories); no retail-specific figure; no net-zero date published.

commodity: Pharmacy and health and beauty retail (multi-site)
operations: Two separate JSE-listed companies. Clicks Group (HO Cnr Searle and Pontac Streets Cape Town): 1 188 stores (877 Clicks SA + 53 rest of Africa, 711 in-store pharmacies, Body Shop, GNC, Sorbet) and UPD wholesale with 8 owned distribution centres (Roodepoort/Lea Glen, Cape Town/Montague Gardens, Durban, Bloemfontein, Gqeberha and others). Dis-Chem Pharmacies (HO Midrand): 358 stores at Feb 2026 (316 Dis-Chem + 42 Baby City) and CJ Distribution with 6 DCs (Longmeadow 63 000 m2, Midrand 44 000 m2, Cape Town, Pinetown, Delmas, Gqeberha); most store and some DC properties are leased, which management says limits ESG capex.
scale_note: Clicks: ~4.5 MW rooftop solar plus lithium batteries at head office and all owned DCs (R105m+ invested), 5 563 MWh generated FY25 = 5.0% of electricity; non-renewable electricity ~108 GWh/yr; Scope 2 99 032 tCO2e FY25; targets 10% renewable electricity by 2030 and carbon neutral by 2050; CDP 2025 response says the group is exploring power purchase agreements to supply renewable energy to the wider store network, and the CEO has cited investment in wheeling and battery storage (Sunday World). Dis-Chem: solar PV at Midrand, Durban and Cape Town DCs (approved May 2024), self-generated renewable 7 419 GJ (~2.1 GWh) in FY2026 = 1.5% of energy; total energy 507 796 GJ FY2026; smart meters rolling out to stores from FY2027; science-based targets being set; no wheeling published.

operations: Privately owned (Fruit & Veg City Holdings; Coppin family with Actis as investor since 2015) - South Africa's largest private retailer. Head office 20 London Circle Brackengate Business Park Brackenfell. More than 120 Food Lover's Market outlets in southern Africa and 22 000 employees (Nov 2025); group also runs FreshStop (330+ forecourt stores at Astron Energy sites), Seattle Coffee, Market Liquors and FVC International. Own Epping and River Club facilities named as next solar sites.
scale_note: Solar generated 5 063 702 kWh in 2024 (+29.9% yoy, 4 572 tCO2e avoided); 9 million kWh generated since launch; over R19m invested in solar with a stated commitment to double it; LED lighting and efficient refrigeration standard in new stores. No wheeling, PPA, GWh consumption or net-zero target published.

operations: Three franchisors. KFC South Africa (Yum! Brands; KFC Africa GM based in Johannesburg): 1 169 restaurants in SA, almost all franchised - the franchisee owns the store electricity account; builds follow Yum's Building Green standards. Famous Brands Ltd (JSE; HO 478 James Crescent Midrand): 2 979 restaurants in 20 countries (3 008 at Aug 2025), only 84 company-owned; owns 10 manufacturing plants and 9 logistics DCs - this vertically integrated supply chain is where the franchisor's own electricity load sits. Spur Corporation (JSE; HO Century City Cape Town): 724 restaurants in 14 countries (619 SA), franchised; only a handful of company-owned restaurants.
scale_note: KFC: no SA energy figures published; Yum target of 46% GHG cut in restaurants and supply chain by 2030 vs 2019. Famous Brands: purchased electricity 31 361 MWh FY25 (manufacturing and logistics) plus ~6 GWh at company-owned restaurants; 1 971 MWh from six solar installations (target 2 400 MWh FY26), two more solar projects due FY26 (Coffee Company and Midrand cold store); exploring a virtual wheeling partnership for green electricity; Scope 1-3 50 509 tCO2e. Spur: Net Zero by 2030 target; reviewing solar, renewable projects and virtual wheeling; franchisee Green Operational Reports track store energy. For a wheeling pitch the counterparties are the franchisees (or landlords), not the franchisor, except Famous Brands' plants and DCs.

commodity: Wholesale and general merchandise / home-improvement retail (multi-site)
operations: Wholly owned by Walmart since the Nov 2022 buy-out and JSE delisting. 273 SA retail units per Walmart corporate site (Makro 23, Builders Warehouse 36, Builders Express 64, Builders Superstore 12, Game 98, Cash & Carry 27, Jumbo 7, Walmart 3); ~300 stores across the region. Game stores are being closed or converted as Walmart-branded stores roll out (first opened Roodepoort Nov 2025). Leadership in transition: two Acting Co-Leads on the leadership page (Sep 2026) after CEO Miles van Rensburg (appointed Mar 2025) dropped off the page.
scale_note: 23 on-site solar plants (five added in the past year) with annual generating capacity of over 11 million kWh; ~52 million kWh generated since the first Makro plants in 2016, ~55 000 tCO2e avoided; individual plants 200 000-1 500 000 kWh/yr sized to daytime load of Makro and Builders big-box stores and DCs; Schneider EcoStruxure building/energy management at 265+ stores (about 20 upgrades a year). Real Estate VP says roll-out continues. No wheeling/PPA or net-zero target published for Massmart; historic electricity consumption ~464 GWh (2015, Greenpeace).

operations: Two JSE-listed groups here (Pepkor people are on the Ackermans record). Mr Price Group (HO 65 Masabalala Yengwa Avenue Durban): more than 3 000 stores, all in landlord-owned premises; Hammarsdale DC 62 000 m2 (expansion capacity to 100 000 m2), Gosforth Park DC reconfiguration (R620m, H2 2026); ~200 new stores a year. TFG / The Foschini Group (HO Stanley Lewis Centre Parow East): 4 923 stores in 23 countries, TFG Africa 3 619 stores in 6 countries; owned and leased DCs incl. the new Riverfields omnichannel DC in Gauteng; owns Prestige Clothing factories.
scale_note: Mr Price: solar at Hammarsdale DC and Durban head office (70% roof coverage) generated 969 403 kWh FY25 = 19.4% of non-store energy; stores retrofitted with LED (85 in FY25) and R208m of battery back-up; Scope 2 82 894 tCO2e FY25 (down from 92 992); explicitly exploring wheeling and renewable energy certificates with key landlords because stores are landlord-owned; climate plan with initial GHG targets approved FY25. TFG: 1.6 MW solar PV installed across TFG Africa facilities; Group Scope 2 ~229 882 tCO2e; Integrated Energy Plan with a new dedicated delivery role; climate change plan aligned to SA NDC 2025-2030; TFG London already on 100% renewable electricity. Neither has published a wheeling deal yet.

operations: Four separately owned networks. Sasol: ~354-400 Sasol-branded retail sites (Mark V forecourt design roll-out), oil-company execs on file elsewhere. Shell South Africa downstream (580-591 sites plus wholesale, aviation, lubricants): sale to ADNOC Distribution for ~US$1bn agreed July 2026, sites to keep the Shell brand under licence. Engen: ~1 040 sites, largest network; Vivo Energy is majority owner (Engen folded into Vivo's ~4 200-site Shell/Engen network) - Vivo says most sites are company-owned but dealer-operated. Astron Energy (Glencore-owned since 2018 Chevron deal): 800+ sites, 700 rebranded from Caltex by Apr 2026; FreshStop convenience partner. Forecourt electricity is generally on the dealer/operator's account at dealer-operated sites, so the oil company is rarely the offtaker; supermarket partners (Woolworths Foodstop ~100 Engen sites, Pick n Pay Express ~188 BP sites, FreshStop 330+ Astron sites) are separate tenants.
scale_note: No forecourt-network solar or wheeling figures published by any of the four; BP (not in this record) is the only brand with an announced 40-site EV/low-carbon upgrade programme. ~3 000 forecourt convenience stores nationally turning over R40bn (2024). No retail-network energy heads published except Astron's retail GM.

commodity: Grocery retail and centralised distribution network
operations: JSE-listed Shoprite Holdings, HO Brackenfell. 3 478 stores in 8 countries of which 2 863 corporate stores; 29 distribution centres with over 900 000 m2 under roof (two new major DCs opened FY25 - Riverfields Gauteng and Wells Estate Gqeberha, +192 900 m2), 1 078 trucks and 1 539 trailers in own fleet; DC capacity partly held via Retail Logistics Fund and Equites. Chief Sustainability Officer role created FY24, reports to the Deputy CEO.
scale_note: Largest private solar portfolio in SA retail: 100th rooftop solar PV system installed Jan 2026, over 43 300 kWp installed; 98 on-site PPAs signed for rooftop generation; renewable 151 243 MWh FY25 = 7.2% of electricity (target met); total energy 2 770 331 MWh FY25; wheeling live at 11 sites incl. Brackenfell home office (via Enpower Trading over the City of Cape Town grid, 2024) and Checkers Newton Park since 2016, Checkers Sitari 100% wind/solar; group says it is actively seeking further wheeling partners and engaging landlords; SBTi-style targets: 42% absolute Scope 1+2 cut by 2030 (2020 base), net zero 2050; Scope 1+2 2.3 Mt CO2e; 1 800 standby diesel generators.

commodity: Grocery wholesale and distribution (voluntary-trading retail network)
operations: JSE-listed SPAR Group; head office moved to The Umhlanga Arch 1 Ncondo Place Umhlanga Ridge Durban (contact page) - the Pinetown address on the record is the old KZN DC/HO. Southern Africa: 2 523 stores (incl. 933 TOPS liquor stores) served by 6 regional DCs plus Build it and S Buys DCs; stores are owned by 2 000+ independent retailers who hold their own electricity accounts, so the group's own load is the DC and warehouse estate. International businesses (Poland, Switzerland, UK) being disposed; Ireland (BWG) retained.
scale_note: Solar PV at all six SA DCs (started South Rand 2017, completed Eastern Cape May 2020): 10 055 623 kWh generated FY25 (2024: 10 419 206 kWh); DC rooftop solar cited as 35%+ savings; exploring gas, wind and biomass to supplement DC solar; net zero across value chain by 2050; total GHG 218 344 tCO2e FY25; Scope 2 rose 23% in FY24 per AGM question. No wheeling/PPA published. Sustainability KPIs in exec incentives.

operations: JSE-listed Woolworths Holdings, HO Woolworths House 93 Longmarket Street Cape Town. Group network 966 stores: Woolworths SA ~430 corporate stores plus 70 Africa corporate stores, Absolute Pets 184 stores, Country Road Group ~270 stores (Australia/NZ); 8 admin buildings and 12 DCs/cross-docks in SA (Midrand and Cape Town DCs). Stores almost all leased. CEO transition: Sam Ngumeni Group CEO from 1 Jun 2026, Roy Bagattini retiring 30 Sep 2026.
scale_note: WHL electricity consumed 338 839 MWh FY25 (WSA 328 591 MWh); self-generated solar 2 498 MWh; renewable share only 2.92% (was 5.88% in FY2023 when WSA took part in the Eskom RET wheeling pilot); head-office solar expanded to 507 kWp (~730 000 kWh/yr); Midrand DC solar (1 MW+ since 2016); two SA stores on landlord-bundled PPAs; FIRST WHEELING AGREEMENT SIGNED in FY25 with a service provider, first tranche expected FY26; targets 100% renewable energy by 2030, net zero Scope 1+2 by 2040 with 50% cut by 2030 (SBTi-approved; 34% below 2019 baseline already); engaging landlords for renewable supply; Section 12L energy-efficiency rebates claimed annually.

operations: JSE-listed City Lodge Hotels, HO The Lodge Bryanston Gate Office Park Bryanston. 58 hotels (City Lodge, Town Lodge, Road Lodge, Courtyard) in South Africa, Botswana, Namibia and Mozambique; owns most of its hotels; debt-free at 30 Jun 2025; Tsogo Sun Limited holds ~12% of the shares. 30% of rooms newly built or refurbished in the last eight years; five more refurbishments planned FY26 (R296.6m capex).
scale_note: Solar PV at 41 of 58 hotels after Phase 2 (Dec 2023): 2.6 MW total generating capacity = 16.3% of group energy requirement; battery storage pilot at two hotels; Phase 3 of solar roll-out initiated FY26 alongside water resilience (boreholes/filtration at 14 hotels); property costs +13.1% FY25 on utility tariffs, partly offset by solar; diesel generator use falling. No wheeling/PPA or net-zero target published.

operations: Two unrelated owners. CTICC (Cape Town International Convention Centre Company SOC Ltd, Convention Square 1 Lower Long Street): municipal entity owned by City of Cape Town 72.7%, Western Cape Provincial Government 22.2%, SunWest International 5.1%; two buildings (CTICC 1 and CTICC 2) linked by a skybridge; electricity supplied by the City of Cape Town; procurement under MFMA supply chain rules. Sandton Convention Centre (Maude Street Sandton, 22 000 m2, 10 000 m2 exhibition space): operated by Southern Sun Ltd (the hotels group unbundled from Tsogo Sun in 2019 - NOT Tsogo Sun Gaming); Southern Sun agreed in Feb 2026 to buy a 50% stake in SCC, Sandton Towers, Garden Court Sandton City and the Virgin Active building from Liberty for R735m; General Manager Shaun Bird.
scale_note: CTICC: total energy 53 142 GJ (~14.8 GWh incl. fuel) in the last published energy page; no rooftop PV yet - solar lights only, PV feasibility study commissioned, Sustainability Manual (2026) says on-site and off-site renewable options still being investigated; BMS, LED (70% of CTICC 1 venue lighting), heat pumps, sub-metering per event; Net Zero Carbon Events pledge: 50% emissions cut by 2030, ISO 14001. SCC: no standalone energy figures published; adjacent Southern Sun Sandton is one of the seven sites in Southern Sun's 10-year Discovery Green wheeling PPA (Jul 2025).

operations: JSE-listed Southern Sun Ltd (formerly Tsogo Sun Hotels, unbundled June 2019; HCI is the controlling shareholder), corporate office Nelson Mandela Square South Tower Maude Street Sandton. 95 hotels and resorts, 16 942 rooms, 300+ conference venues in SA, Africa, Seychelles and UAE; owns or leases 81 hotels (89% of rooms) incl. 76 owned in South Africa, manages 14 for third parties; also operates Sandton Convention Centre and is buying a 50% stake in the Sandton precinct assets from Liberty (R735m, Feb 2026). Net debt only R266m at Mar 2025; R450m refurbishment capex FY25.
scale_note: Signed a 10-YEAR WHEELING PPA with Discovery Green (18 Jul 2025) covering more than 90% of consumption at seven flagship sites - Arabella Hotel Golf & Spa, Drakensberg Sun, Garden Court Morningside, Southern Sun Katherine Street, Southern Sun Sandton, Champagne Sports Resort, Sabi River Sun - supplied from wind and solar incl. Overberg Wind Farm phase 2 via the national grid; electricity cost rose R37m in FY25 on tariffs while diesel fell R36m; property-level environmental management systems, 20 boreholes; first standalone CDP submission scored B; climate transition plan being developed for IFRS S2; no group MW-of-solar or GWh figure published in the IAR.

operations: JSE-listed Sun International, HO Sandton. Nine urban casinos (GrandWest, Sun Time Square, Sibaya, Carnival City, Boardwalk, Meropa, Windmill, Flamingo, Golden Valley), resorts and hotels (Sun City, Wild Coast Sun, The Maslow Sandton), Sun Slots LPMs and Sunbet online; The Table Bay Hotel exited 2025. New CE Ulrik Bengtsson from 1 Jul 2025 with new COOs for Gaming and Hospitality appointed H2 2025. Proposed Peermont acquisition (announced Dec 2023) not approved by competition authorities.
scale_note: Grid electricity ~198.6 GWh (2024: 198 627 309 kWh); on-site solar generated 4 915 706 kWh in 2024 = ~2% of consumption from Sun City (1.6 MW Sun Central rooftop commissioned Jul 2023 plus further plants), Carnival City and Sibaya (2024 commissioning; 2025 first full year of data); 1 MW battery storage at The Maslow Sandton (Feb 2024); R150m board-approved green-energy capex 2023-24; Boardwalk Mall solar R5m 2025; ESG report 2024 states the group will investigate WHEELING agreements in 2025 for Eskom- and municipality-supplied operations, for supply in 2026; net zero by 2050; R2.4bn sustainability-linked loan with a renewable-energy KPI; bulk metering at all units.

commodity: Casino hotel and spa (site of Tsogo Sun Limited)
operations: Site record: The Caledon Casino Hotel & Spa in the Overberg - 95-room 3-star hotel, casino, Victorian bathhouse and spa, three restaurants, four venues up to 120 delegates. Owner is Tsogo Sun Limited (JSE; 50% HCI; HO Palazzo Towers East Montecasino Boulevard Fourways) - the casino/gaming company that is separate from Southern Sun (hotels) since June 2019, so group executives are attached here. Group: 14 casino precincts (Montecasino, Gold Reef City, Suncoast, Silverstar, Emerald, Caledon, Mykonos, Garden Route, etc.), 24 Galaxy Bingo sites, VSlots LPMs, bet.co.za/playTSOGO. Caledon trading weak: FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA down double digits, goodwill impaired R40m (FY25 R24m), recoverable amount R105m; Tsogo Sun has regulatory approval to relocate a Western Cape casino licence to Somerset West/Helderberg (under court review) - check whether this is Caledon's licence before investing sales effort.
scale_note: Group has installed rooftop solar for daytime use at several precincts: Montecasino and Gold Reef City plants expanded, and new plants at Gold Reef City Theme Park, Emnotweni, The Ridge and Blackrock completed Feb 2025; solar capex programme described as mostly complete; no Caledon-specific solar published; Scope 2 emissions rose 8% FY25 on higher grid use as load shedding eased; utility cost inflation cited as offsetting solar benefit; no wheeling/PPA or net-zero date published; no MW total disclosed.
